name: Browser Use Cloud

modes.label: Browser runtime
modes.note: Plus bandwidth; proxy enabled by default. Running browser remains billable after agent run/CDP disconnect. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee. Credits for the requested timeout (default 60 min, max 240) are reserved at creation and unused time refunded at stop; final charge rounded up to whole minute, 1-min min. Top-ups $5-$100,000 whole dollars, presets $100/$500/$1,000. API-key monthly spend caps are soft limits. EU (Frankfurt) deployment: same billing/balance, EU-only proxy countries (default de), automatic CAPTCHA solving disabled, standalone custom proxy unavailable.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: No subscription; $5 minimum top-up; never expires. Spend-tier concurrency separate.

plans.name: Spend tier 50
plans.note: Requires $200 qualifying lifetime payments per pricing page and pricing.md ('Tier 1 | $200 | 50'); concurrency docs and docs llms.txt still say $100 (conflict persists 2026-09-29). Not a monthly fee.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom concurrency (1,000+), custom SLA, HIPAA/ZDR, dedicated support, negotiated annual credit pool (commitment), EU data residency on request. Same $0.02/browser-hour list rates.

free.note: One-time $15 for eligible Google/GitHub/Microsoft signups (email/password excluded), no card; free accounts limited to cost-efficient models and no auto-recharge; first top-up ($5 min) unlocks all models.

features.ip_note: US residential proxy on by default ($5/GB, country selectable); custom/BYO proxy on all accounts, then traffic billed $0.20/GB.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
No current Dev/Business/Scaleup subscriptions offered; older comparisons are obsolete for new buyers. Legacy concurrency grants can be preserved.

Concurrency is lifetime purchased-credit spend, not monthly fee. Card cannot enforce a historical spend gate; the zero-fee higher tiers must not be auto-selected without checking account qualification.
Pricing page says $200 lifetime spend unlocks 50 sessions; docs says $100. Keep both and inspect account grant before purchasing solely for concurrency.

V 4 agent browsers have four-hour hard timeout and roughly 20-minute idle cleanup after inactive runs. An eight-hour single session is not valid for that product; standalone browser limits may differ.
No 4/8 guarantee; model prices are separate token meters, not compute. Managed token prices already include the 20% fee; do not add it twice.

Browser create API reserves the full requested runtime amount up front, refunding unused duration at stop proportionally; final billing remains rounded up to whole minutes. A prepaid wallet must cover the initial reservation.
V4 per-run spend caps scale per model up to $100 (changelog 2026-08-10); x402 (USDC on Base) pay-per-request top-ups from $0.01 to $100 with no account; BYOK cache-read overcharge fixed 2026-08-24.

fleet.verification: Eligible Google/GitHub/Microsoft signup gets introductory credits without card. Paid tiers use net settled lifetime Stripe payments per project; refunds, disputes and grants excluded.
fleet.tiers: 10 at $0; 50 at $200 lifetime spend on pricing page versus $100 in concurrency docs (conflict); 250 at $1,000; 500 at $5,000; 1,000 at $25,000. Custom Enterprise by contact.
fleet.notes: Browser and agent runs share project concurrency; more API keys do not add capacity. Qualifying cumulative purchases, not monthly fee or current wallet balance. Higher legacy grants preserved. Because first threshold conflicts, confirm project Billing/API limit before buying solely to raise it; no guaranteed processing time. HTTP request limits separate from concurrency: per-project general bucket (creates/lists/updates/deletes) = max(25, 2x concurrency) RPS capped at 100 RPS; status reads max(25, 2x concurrency) uncapped; edge WAF 1,000 RPS per source IP (raised 2026-09-09). Tier 0 (10 sessions) = 25 RPS floor. Start rate is not a practical constraint at <=1,000 sessions.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.note: The full V4 OpenAPI path list (runs, sessions, workspaces, browsers, profiles, integrations, share, wallets) has no snapshot/checkpoint/fork endpoint; the product is a managed Chrome over CDP plus a hosted agent. Nearest analogues: saved profiles (cookies/localStorage) that new browsers can load, and workspaces reused across sessions. No memory snapshot.

own_agent_api.quote: Use the session queue to send the next instruction without interrupting the active run.
own_agent_api.note: Harness = Browser Use's own hosted browser agent (API V4; legacy V2/V3). REST+Python/TS SDK: POST /runs with a task (choice of Claude/GPT/Gemini/Grok/GLM etc. models), GET /runs/{id}/events ("Paginated event read. `after` is the event id cursor"), follow-ups via sessionId or POST /sessions/{id}/queue (interrupt or queue), list/get/delete/share sessions, cancel run. Does not drive Claude Code/Codex inside the sandbox; those are integrations that call Browser Use as a tool.

harness_api.quote: Use the session queue to send the next instruction without interrupting the active run.
harness_api.note: Harness = Browser Use's own hosted browser agent (API V4; legacy V2/V3). REST+Python/TS SDK: POST /runs with a task (choice of Claude/GPT/Gemini/Grok/GLM etc. models), GET /runs/{id}/events ("Paginated event read. `after` is the event id cursor"), follow-ups via sessionId or POST /sessions/{id}/queue (interrupt or queue), list/get/delete/share sessions, cancel run. Does not drive Claude Code/Codex inside the sandbox; those are integrations that call Browser Use as a tool.

guest_firewall.note: The customer gets a managed Chrome over CDP (or a hosted agent), no shell/root in the underlying machine, so cannot run nftables/iptables. Not stated explicitly in docs.

secret_proxy.quote: Aliases avoid putting raw credentials in the task text. They do not guarantee that the agent cannot see the value: once typed, it is accessible to the page and to an agent with browser/CDP access.
secret_proxy.note: V4 secretBindings / 1Password vault bindings are typed into the page server-side by alias on allowed domains (the LLM never reads the value: 'Credentials this run may use without ever seeing them'), but the real value enters the browser, so it is not a network-level credential-injecting proxy. HTTP only (form fields); no DB/SSH/git.

volume_attach.quote: The current V4 upload allowance is 950 MiB per workspace for every account, with 50 MiB per file. It leaves room for runtime files on the agent's 1 GiB persistent disk.
volume_attach.note: No attachable block/network volumes. Workspaces are object-storage file sets synced into runs (950 MiB quota), not mounted volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Workspace files are synchronized to storage between runs. This is not a live shared filesystem between simultaneous sessions: finish one writer before starting another run that needs its changes.
volume_shared.note: A workspace can be reused by several sessions but only via sync between runs, not concurrent mounts.

image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Customers get a fixed managed Chromium instance via CDP/API; there is no way to start a machine from a custom Docker/OCI image.

docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No shell/root access to the underlying machine is exposed, so containers cannot be run inside it.

nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No /dev/kvm or shell access is exposed to customers.

desktop.quote: Live view and streaming. Every session exposes a live URL you can embed for human review or takeover, and a recording for audit.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The live view streams the browser tab only (no VNC/RDP full desktop with a window manager/taskbar).

ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Access is via CDP/REST/SDK only; no SSH into the underlying machine is documented.

snapshot.quote: The full V4 OpenAPI path list (runs, sessions, workspaces, browsers, profiles, integrations, share, wallets) has no snapshot/checkpoint/fork endpoint
snapshot.note: Nearest analogues are browser profiles (cookies/localStorage) and workspaces (files), neither of which is a disk or memory snapshot/restore of the whole machine.

snapshot_auto.note: No automatic save/restore of machine state on stop/sleep is documented; the API has no such mechanism.

fork.note: No clone/fork endpoint exists in the V4 API surface.

fork_running.note: No fork capability at all, so cloning a running machine is not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork capability at all, so memory-preserving forks are not offered.

pause_resume.quote: Running browser remains billable after agent run/CDP disconnect.
pause_resume.note: A browser session runs until stopped or it times out; no pause/resume (paused or reduced billing) API is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Running browser remains billable after agent run/CDP disconnect.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no stopped/sleeping-machine-wakes-on-request mechanism; sessions are created fresh via the API and time out rather than sleeping and auto-waking.

persistent_disk.quote: Workspace files are synchronized to storage between runs.
persistent_disk.note: Workspace files (up to 950 MiB) and browser profiles (cookies/localStorage/login state) persist across runs/sessions, which is the functional equivalent of a persistent disk for this product, though it is object storage rather than a literal attached disk.

live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Browser-hour billing has no customer-selectable/resizable CPU/RAM; there is no VM sizing concept exposed.

agent_harnesses.quote: Browser Harness gives Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Hermes Agent, and OpenClaw a real browser: the developer's own logged-in Chrome locally, or Browser Use stealth browsers in the cloud, driven through CDP
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Browser Use is consumed as a tool BY external coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, etc.); it does not preinstall/offer those harnesses running inside its own sandbox.

mcp_server.quote: Run browser automation tasks from your AI coding assistant. Connect to Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, or any MCP client. https://api.browser-use.com/v3/mcp
mcp_server.note: First-party hosted MCP server exposing browser automation tools.

lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK (browser-use-sdk, with a v4 import) for driving the cloud API.

lang_node.note: First-party TypeScript/Node SDK (browser-use-sdk) for driving the cloud API.

public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Customers reach the managed browser only via a CDP/live-view URL issued by Browser Use, not a dedicated public IPv4 address per machine.

inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no concept of exposing arbitrary customer-run ports/services over HTTPS; the only HTTPS/WSS endpoints are the provider's own CDP/live-view/API URLs.

ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No customer ports are exposed at all, so there is nothing to apply ingress access rules to.

egress_allowlist.quote: Domain allow and block lists. Restrict a session to allowed_domains or exclude prohibited_domains.
egress_allowlist.note: Provider-side outbound domain allow/deny lists for browser sessions.

egress_http_rules.quote: Domain allow and block lists. Restrict a session to allowed_domains or exclude prohibited_domains.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is domain-level only; no documented method/path-level HTTP egress rules.

static_egress_ip.quote: Residential proxies in 195+ countries, country selection per session, and bring-your-own proxy.
static_egress_ip.note: Managed proxies are residential/rotating with country selection, not a fixed provider-assigned outbound IP; a fixed IP would require the customer's own BYO proxy, which is not Browser Use's own static egress IP.

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The product is a managed browser runtime, not a compute/VM product; no GPU machine option is documented.

windows.quote: Per-session fingerprints. Canvas, WebGL, fonts, navigator, and other signals are randomized per session, with macOS, Windows, and Linux fingerprint sets.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Windows/macOS are only simulated browser fingerprints for anti-detection; the underlying hosted machine running the browser is not a selectable Windows machine.

macos.quote: Per-session fingerprints. Canvas, WebGL, fonts, navigator, and other signals are randomized per session, with macOS, Windows, and Linux fingerprint sets.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. macOS is only a simulated browser fingerprint, not an actual macOS machine offered to run on.

arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The product abstracts away machine architecture entirely; there is no customer-selectable ARM option.

byoc.quote: Enterprise agreements add custom concurrency, custom SLAs, dedicated support, negotiated annual credit pools, and a custom data policy.
byoc.note: Enterprise features cover compliance/SLA/data policy, not deployment into the customer's own cloud account; no BYOC option is documented.

sso.quote: SOC 2 Type II. Audited by an independent firm; report available under NDA.
sso.note: The enterprise/security page lists SOC 2, HIPAA, DPA, and data controls in detail but never mentions SAML/OIDC single sign-on for dashboard login; not documented as offered.

eu_data_residency.quote: EU data residency for browsers and agents is available to enterprise customers on request.
eu_data_residency.note: Also reflected in the EU (Frankfurt) deployment described on the pricing/eu-deployment docs.

usage_api.quote: Running browser remains billable after agent run/CDP disconnect. Credits for the requested timeout (default 60 min, max 240) are reserved at creation and unused time refunded at stop; final charge rounded up to whole minute, 1-min min.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; Browser Use Cloud API (V4 REST+SDK) provides session/run management (POST /runs, GET /runs/{id}/events, POST /sessions/{id}/queue, list/get/delete/share sessions) but no documented endpoint to retrieve billable usage/credits spent per sandbox/run/session. Billing is dashboard/invoice-only; no usage breakdown API.

locations_quote: EU (Frankfurt) deployment: same billing/balance, EU-only proxy countries (default de), automatic CAPTCHA solving disabled, standalone custom proxy unavailable.
